Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking the call this morning. As part of our procurement checklist (attached), our privacy team needs two concrete things before we can sign: a short evidence pack that demonstrates Redwood's operational controls for "we do not train on customer data", and a clear statement of any retention/deletion exceptions (logs, snapshots, backups, debugging traces) that might persist beyond our requested deletion timeline.

Concretely - can you provide:
- A one-page attestation we can include in our security binder confirming production data is not used for model training (if possible, signed)
- A matrix that lists types of telemetry/logs, retention TTLs, and whether any of those are exempt from immediate deletion requests (e.g., backups kept for legal/regulatory reasons)
- Confirmation of whether KV cache or ephemeral traces are ever persisted to long-term storage that could be used in retraining

I've attached our security_questionnaire_v3.xlsx and highlighted relevant rows. We are aiming to close by the end of next week.

Appreciate the help — Laura

Folks — drafting updates below and attaching a short checklist I've started. See attached 'requested_evidence_checklist.pdf'. Notes:

- Attestation: We can provide a signed "No Training on Customer Data" attestation for FinCo for hosted and dedicated tiers, and for Private deployments when the control plane is under Redwood management. For self-hosted Private installs where the customer runs the inference stack entirely in their environment, we will document that Redwood has no operational access.

- Retention matrix (high level):
  * Request payloads (customer API text): default retention = ephemeral (24 hours) for telemetry-only, retained longer only if customer opts-in to logging or if account-level audit logging is enabled (TTL configurable). Not used for training.
  * KV cache / inference cache: in-memory, TTL per-session; not persisted to long-term storage.
  * Debug snapshots & crash dumps: retained up to 90 days, encrypted at rest, access-controlled, used solely for debugging; can be excluded per-request if customer requests stricter retention in contract.
  * Backups & snapshots (system-level): retained per our backup policy (30-90 days depending on tier); subject to legal holds; backups are not used for training.
  * Aggregated telemetry (usage metrics, anonymized latency/cost stats): retained up to 24 months for platform improvement; this dataset is strictly aggregated and hashed — not taggable to raw customer content for training.

- Edge case: derivative synthetic datasets generated for internal benchmarks are always synthetic or open-source only; we do not mix customer content into benchmark training sets.

I'll produce a PDF attestation and a table that maps each artifact to TTLs and a short rationale. Priyom — can you confirm with runtime engineering whether any debug traces are ever egressed to long-term blob storage beyond the 90d window?

Mina

On Tue, Nov 10, 2026 at 09:23, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Priyom — can you confirm with runtime engineering whether any debug traces are ever egressed to long-term blob storage beyond the 90d window?

Quick update from runtime: default flow keeps debug snapshots in encrypted ephemeral buckets with 90d lifecycle. Two known exceptions:
1) Support-generated archives for a customer investigation are archived to long-term storage (365d) when the customer requests extended debugging and signs an access/retention addendum.
2) Region-level redundancy backups (scheduled weekly system snapshots) may be retained for up to 180 days depending on the Dedicated plan and the underlying cloud provider retention settings. These backups are treated as system backups and are explicitly excluded from any training pipelines.

Action items:
- We'll include both exceptions in the retention matrix and flag the two flows that require a customer-facing addendum.
- We'll attach a draft attestation (no_train_attestation_signed.pdf) for signature by legal. Mina — please coordinate sign-off.

Priyom
